prerequisites: Basic knowledge of high-level programming languages, e.g., in C/C++

learning_outcomes.text: After completing this module, students will have basic knowledge of the design and testing of digital circuits and their mapping to programmable logic devices using hardware description languages.

Graduates understand alternative design methodologies and can assess the underlying principles and methods. They are able to deepen their knowledge independently, taking into account current developments.
Students are able to analyze, design, and optimize combinatorial and sequential circuits.
Students are able to assess the functionality of digital components in an overall system and to develop and implement new digital systems.
After completing the module, students can select suitable methods for the design of digital circuits for a given task and explain and discuss the design process.

syllabus_topics: Simulation, testing and synthesis with an integrated development environment
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is a written exam. The ungraded assessment is experimental work, consisting of approximately 5 experiments, each 90 minutes long. The duration of the written exam is defined by the valid study regulations.
bibliography: W. Gehrke, M. Winzker: Digitaltechnik. Springer-Verlag, 8. Auflage, 2023.
Peter J. Ashenden: The Designer's Guide to VHDL. Morgan Kaufmann, 2008.
